clue.text: Gets money, changing this in a letter!

definitions.text: Gets money, changing this in a letter!

parts.words: Gets money, changing this in a letter!
parts.note: a mailed money voucher is cashed at the post office by whoever receives the envelope, so 'gets money' by exchanging it

explanation.surface: Someone receives cash by swapping something tucked into their mail.
explanation.walkthrough: A POSTAL ORDER is a British money voucher bought at a post office and sent through the mail; the recipient changes it for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description of a money voucher sent by post and cashed by the person who receives the envelope.

clue.text: Place for Speakers of the House?

definitions.text: Place for Speakers of the House?

parts.words: Place for Speakers of the House?
parts.note: the room's name comes from French parler, to speak, so it is literally a speaking room of a house

explanation.surface: A question about where the Speaker of the House of Commons sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speakers of the House' suggests Parliament, but it means anyone in a home who talks: the word derives from French parler, to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room in a home, historically the room set aside for conversation with visitors.

clue.text: Being old-fashioned, loves this lad

definitions.text: Being old-fashioned, loves this lad

parts.words: Being old-fashioned, loves this lad
parts.note: an archaic or poetic word for a young country lover or suitor, so a lad who loves, in old-fashioned language

explanation.surface: A girl with traditional ways falls for a particular young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic, dated term for a young male suitor or country youth.

clue.text: The chief — how he helps his subordinate

definitions.text: The chief — how he helps his subordinate

parts.words: The chief — how he helps his subordinate
parts.note: read as a description of how a boss aids an underling, but really an assistant's job description turned round: the chief is the one doing the helping

explanation.surface: A remark on the way a boss supports a junior member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: One normally thinks of a subordinate helping the chief; here the chief does the helping, giving the plain verb for lending a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain verb for gives help or aids, the thing the chief does for his subordinate.

clue.text: Runs away from home just for fun!

definitions.text: Runs away from home just for fun!

parts.words: Runs away from home just for fun!
parts.note: sounds like a child absconding, but means pleasure trips: excursions away from the house taken for enjoyment

explanation.surface: A child who leaves home on a whim, for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs away' suggests escape, but a run is also a short trip, so these are jaunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Short pleasure trips or excursions, i.e. leisure jaunts away from the house.

clue.text: What the boss says will be correspondence from his secretary

definitions.text: What the boss says will be correspondence from his secretary

parts.words: What the boss says will be correspondence from his secretary
parts.note: the words a manager speaks aloud for a typist to take down later become the letters she sends

explanation.surface: An office where the manager's words end up as letters typed by an assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Words spoken to be written down by another, such as a boss's letters taken down in shorthand.

clue.text: Moving the stock in trade of the railway company

definitions.text: Moving
definitions.meaning: travelling along, turning over and over, in motion

definitions.text: the stock in trade of the railway company
definitions.meaning: railway carriages and wagons are called the ... stock, so this word is what qualifies a railway's stock

explanation.surface: A railway firm's goods are being transported somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: First sense: in motion; second: the word paired with 'stock' to name a railway's carriages and wagons.

clue.text: Cries, coming out of the torture-chamber

definitions.text: Cries, coming out of the torture-chamber

parts.words: Cries, coming out of the torture-chamber
parts.note: the shrieks heard from a dungeon where people are tortured

explanation.surface: Sounds of anguish heard from a medieval dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud piercing cries of pain or terror, the shrieks one hears from victims.

clue.text: Rubber needing a special abrasive to make it catch light!

definitions.text: Rubber needing a special abrasive to make it catch light!

parts.words: Rubber needing a special abrasive to make it catch light!
parts.note: a match that strikes only on the special rough strip of its own box: a thing rubbed that needs a particular surface to ignite

explanation.surface: Sounds like tyre rubber or an eraser being sanded until it bursts into flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' means something that is rubbed or struck, not the elastic material.
explanation.definitionFit: A match designed to ignite only when struck on the specially prepared strip on its box.

clue.text: Tried to stop one playing rugby

definitions.text: Tried
definitions.meaning: attempted, took on a task or problem

definitions.text: to stop one playing rugby
definitions.meaning: brought down a ball-carrier in rugby

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to halt a rugby player in full flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: set about dealing with something, and brought down an opponent carrying the ball.

clue.text: Author to rewrite file on dead one? No, omits it

definitions.text: Author

indicators.note: rewriting the words means jumbling their letters into a new order

parts.words: file on dead one
No
parts.note: the word as printed, whose letters are the ones left out

explanation.surface: A writer is told to redo a document about a deceased person, then told not to.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange FILE ON DEAD ONE but 'omits' the letters of NO: the remaining eleven letters spell the author of Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.definitionFit: English writer of Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders, so an example of an author.

clue.text: Escaped-being taken between airports!

definitions.text: Escaped
definitions.meaning: fled, got away, as a bird has left its nest

definitions.text: being taken between airports
definitions.meaning: carried by aircraft from one airfield to another

explanation.surface: Someone got away by being moved by plane between airfields.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: having fled, as in 'the bird has gone', and transported by aircraft.

clue.text: We feel it will arouse great public interest and excitement

definitions.text: We feel it
definitions.meaning: a physical feeling or perception received through the senses

definitions.text: will arouse great public interest and excitement
definitions.meaning: a stir or event that causes a great public furore

explanation.surface: A sensational event causes widespread excitement among people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a bodily feeling or perception, and an event creating a public stir.

clue.text: Has confidence in how the head drives

definitions.text: drives

indicators.note: the word 'in' places the single letter inside the verb for having confidence

parts.words: Has confidence
parts.note: to have confidence in someone is to trust them

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of 'how'

parts.words: how

explanation.surface: A remark on believing in the way a headmaster runs the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has confidence in' looks like one phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'how the head' gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: Drives as a noun means forceful pushes or lunges, which is the sense of the plural noun here.

clue.text: Hull, with all its dockyard accoutrements, belongs to him

definitions.text: Hull, with all its dockyard accoutrements, belongs to him

parts.words: Hull, with all its dockyard accoutrements, belongs to him
parts.note: a vessel's hull plus its fittings make a vessel, and the person it belongs to is its owner

explanation.surface: Sounds like the port city of Hull and its docks being owned by one man.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England, but here a hull is a vessel's body.
explanation.definitionFit: Person who owns a vessel, i.e. the proprietor of a seagoing craft.

clue.text: In America, a sign advertising "On the Beach"; but it's cut!

definitions.text: In America, a sign advertising "On the Beach"; but it's cut!

parts.words: In America, a sign advertising "On the Beach"; but it's cut!
parts.note: three senses: an American signboard of a professional, the pebbles on a beach, and a short tapered haircut

explanation.surface: An American billboard promotes a seaside venue but has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US a professional 'hangs out a shingle', a small signboard; the word also means beach pebbles and a 1920s cropped hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: a small US signboard, beach pebbles, and a short layered haircut.

clue.text: Dog goes up on sailing ship, if on foot first

definitions.text: Dog

parts.words: goes up on sailing ship
parts.note: the tall spar that rises from the deck of a sailing vessel

parts.words: if
parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: foot

explanation.surface: A dog climbs a sailing ship's rigging, provided it goes by foot first.
explanation.definitionFit: A large powerful breed of guard dog, so one example of the canine.

clue.text: Something threatening your life? So, come out quick!

definitions.text: Something threatening your life? So, come out quick!

parts.words: Something threatening your life? So, come out quick!
parts.note: quick in its old sense means alive, so to come through a danger still alive

explanation.surface: Urgent advice to flee fast from something deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like 'fast' but carries the old sense of living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain alive through a danger, coming out of it still living.

clue.text: Battered one to waste his money

definitions.text: Battered one
definitions.meaning: a piece of fruit or meat coated in batter and fried

definitions.text: to waste his money
definitions.meaning: to squander funds gradually on trifles

explanation.surface: A beaten-up man is going to throw his cash away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' suggests beaten up, but means coated in batter and fried.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a deep-fried morsel in batter and a verb meaning squander gradually.

clue.text: Caused pain in flesh between the fingers

definitions.text: Caused pain in flesh between the fingers

parts.words: Caused pain in flesh between the fingers
parts.note: squeezing skin tightly between finger and thumb hurts

explanation.surface: Someone hurt another by squeezing skin between their fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezed skin sharply between finger and thumb, causing pain.

clue.text: Opts out, having cracked up after wartime conference here

definitions.text: wartime conference here

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the word are knocked out of order

parts.words: Opts

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.words: cracked
parts.note: cracked means crazy, mad

explanation.surface: Someone opts out after a breakdown following a wartime summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' means crazy here; in a down clue 'up' reads a word from the bottom, and 'Opts out' looks like a choice not to join, but 'out' only jumbles the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: German city near Berlin that hosted the 1945 Allied summit, the place of that wartime conference.

clue.text: Will had her name down for "Great Expectations" when she'd finished "Hard Times," perhaps!

definitions.text: Will had her name down for "Great Expectations" when she'd finished "Hard Times," perhaps!

parts.words: Will had her name down for "Great Expectations" when she'd finished "Hard Times," perhaps!
parts.note: a woman named in a testament can expect a large inheritance once her own lean years are over; 'Will' is a legal document, not a man

explanation.surface: A literary anecdote about a man called Will and two Dickens novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a man's name but is a testament; the Dickens titles stand for hopes of a fortune and poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman due to inherit wealth, having been named in someone's testament.

clue.text: The end of his violent career to bring political change

definitions.text: The end of his violent career to bring political change

parts.words: The end of his violent career to bring political change
parts.note: the aim of a man who uses bombs and violence is to force a change of government

explanation.surface: A violent man's life story whose purpose was political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end' looks like the conclusion of a career, but means its aim or purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Person who uses violence against civilians to achieve political aims.

clue.text: Goes straight down to the beach at Dover

definitions.text: Goes straight down to the beach at Dover

parts.words: Goes straight down to the beach at Dover
parts.note: the famous white chalk faces at Dover drop sheer to the shore

explanation.surface: Directions for heading directly to Dover's seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover, on England's south coast, is famous for its white chalk sea faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep rock face dropping sheer to the sea, such as the white chalk ones at Dover.

clue.text: Trees not taking up much space!

definitions.text: Trees not taking up much space!

parts.words: Trees not taking up much space!
parts.note: a small group of trees, a little wood covering only a small area

explanation.surface: A remark about trees that fit into a small plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thicket or stand of trees, a little wood occupying modest ground.

clue.text: In order to keep them, locks fastened all round!

definitions.text: In order to keep them, locks fastened all round!

parts.words: In order to keep them, locks fastened all round!
parts.note: a mesh worn over hair keeps the locks tidy, enclosing them on every side

explanation.surface: Sounds like a building secured by bolting every door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door fastenings, but means tresses of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the head to hold the hair in place.

clue.text: Put down what's in store for you!

definitions.text: Put down what's in store for you!

parts.words: Put down what's in store for you!
parts.note: to reduce or use up stocks is to bring down the amount held in reserve

explanation.surface: A threat or prophecy about one's future fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's in store' sounds like fate, but means stocks kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up or reduce supplies, lowering what is held in reserve.

clue.text: Found it hard to listen, people using such amplifiers

definitions.text: Found it hard to listen, people using such amplifiers

parts.words: Found it hard to listen, people using such amplifiers
parts.note: old horn-shaped devices held up to the head by the hard of hearing to magnify sound

explanation.surface: Inattentive people turned to loud sound equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned horn-shaped hearing aids that amplify sound for the deaf.
